groups.problem: The getBaseConditions branches that handle falsy authConditions (returning filterConditions alone, or NOTHING_CONDITION) are wrong: unreachable, or a latent auth bypass.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `getBaseConditions` returns `filterConditions` alone (no authorization predicate) when `authConditions` is falsy (`else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`). HOW: Always AND the authorization predicate with the filters and fall back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` when no auth predicate exists, e.g. `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;` (or keep the `NOTHING_CONDITION` default when auth is missing).

suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The exclusive lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer on line 49) across the blocking file read / synchronous CDN HTTP request (lines 56-67) and there is no re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock. The comment says the grant shortcut starts at the 4th character, and substring(3,5) follows it. The token ID format is sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2), so the shortcut is at indices 4-6, i.e. substring(4,6). Fix the offset and the comment so they match the encoded format.

isAccessTokenId never checks the grant type. It reads substring(3, 5) when the grant shortcut is at indices 4..6, and it returns false when the shortcut matches instead of when it differs. As written the check never rejects anything, so event assertions pass even with the wrong or an unknown grant shortcut. Use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.
